title: Size of the move (2/4): the size record, its proxy guard, and the sizePolicy preference
description:
## As asked

Piece 2 of 4 of LIN-4346 ("Deciding the size of the move becomes part of the run"). Code only: who runs scoping does not change here. Lands after piece 1.

**Why.** This week's mistakes came from hand-off scope that said *how* (Finding 9 in `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md`). The written size must be what and why only, and code, not only prompt wording, has to hold that line. How big the move is stays a person's call, given as a ruling or as a standing policy set once.

**This piece's slice of the approved plan**

* **One module owns the record** (`lib/size-of-move.js` or similar): the heading `## Size of the move`; the closed list of sizes (just the task / a small tidy / consolidate the decision this task touches / rebuild the area / wrong work); the decided-by values (a ruling / the standing policy / pending a ruling); a parser that reads only the description below the As-asked block (`outsideAsAsked`), never comments; and the check. The scoping prompt, facts line, guard, code route and close-out prune all take their vocabulary from it.
* **What a record says:** the chosen size in plain words and why; the sizes weighed, as one-line bullets on what each buys this task; the extra and when it may stop, if larger; each cut quoted with its ruling, or none; who decided.
* **The guard** sits beside `refusedByAsAsked` at both description-write call sites in `routes/proxy-writes.js` (`:478`, `:566` at the base). It acts only when a write adds or changes the section, and refuses with a line-specific 422 for: file paths, code spans, call syntax, or numbered steps in the section (exempt: a quotation matching As-asked text word for word); "the standing policy" deciding "wrong work"; a write that drops an existing section. An unchanged older section never blocks an unrelated write. Document the refusal codes in `lib/proxy-instructions.js` beside AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE. Session-lane and direct provider edits stay people's lanes.
* **Close-out keeps the record:** the prune step (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js:1063` at the base) keeps the section verbatim.
* **The policy:** workspace preference `sizePolicy`, `ask` (default) or `err-larger`, stored with who set it and when, in `lib/workspace-preferences.js` beside `dispatchDefaults`. Set from Settings → Running (`lib/settings-areas.js`): register the POST route in the area's `routes` census and show the current policy in its `state`. One loader, called from `prepareRecommendationInput` (`lib/recommendation-input.js`) and the pinned-kind path in `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, so both scoping-render paths carry it. `err-larger` = take the larger move when the look shows it pays and when in doubt; not inflating every ticket.
* **Facts line:** the selector's trail facts gain "Size of the move: not recorded / pending a ruling / chosen X (by …)".

**Testing strategy / witness** (each guard test fails before this piece)

* Refused: a section with a path, a backticked helper, or "1. … 2. …"; a policy-decided "wrong work"; a write that drops the section. Finding 9's hand-offs as fixtures: wherever they carried how, the guard refuses them.
* Permitted: plain what-and-why prose; bullet options; a quoted cut whose quote carries a code span from the ask block (while the same span not in the ask block is refused); a write that leaves an old section alone.
* Parser: a ticket whose only `## Size of the move` is a comment reads as not recorded.
* Close-out prune retains the section.
* Settings census passes with the new key and route.
* A scoping prompt rendered through both entrances shows the policy when set and "no standing policy" when not.

**Session fit:** fits one session.

**Plan-review due:** no — covered by LIN-4346's approving plan-review (comment d71c7085-b2ad-4760-8070-53bc917f9a1f, rev 1).

**Grounding commit:** `11dc1d7bd` (`origin/main` when the plan was written and reviewed; still `origin/main` at breakdown, 7 Nov 22:45 UTC).

**Starting point:** LIN-4346's approved plan is this piece's starting point. Read it in full in LIN-4346's description under `## Implementation Plan` (revision 1), with the builder notes in the approving verdict (comment d71c7085, 22:42). Read LIN-4346's `## As asked` block for the person's words and John's comment of 22:18 for the size ruling (err larger). Follow the plan; where the code shows it wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4346.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implemented

Implemented in PR [#2355](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2355>), squash commit `eeda7e44`, deployed to [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>). The approved plan (LIN-4346, revision 1) was implemented with the changes of course review accepted: four render paths, logged and undoable policy changes, and Running state that always names the policy. Close-out added a fifth render entrance (the in-app prompt route) and made the policy-cut check read every size section. One operator check remains: the Settings → Running round trip, which ends by setting err-larger (see the close-out comment). The full history is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

parent.title: Deciding the size of the move becomes part of the run

comments.body: LIN-4367 (1/4), which blocked this ticket, has merged as `9c2a378a` (PR #2354) and is deployed. This piece now builds on that simpler shape. Notes for whoever builds it: the budget file keeps only the latest ticket and reason beside each ceiling, and the history lives in `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` under `## Ceiling history`. `CUT` and `DECIDE` are now exported from `lib/prompts/stage-intent.js`.

Piece 2 is in review: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2355. The head is `e91d62c0`, and CI is green: `ci-success`, unit tests, all four E2E shards and the secret scan.

**What landed**
- **One owner for the record.** `lib/size-of-move.js` owns the heading, the closed list of sizes, the decided-by values, the policy values, a parser that reads only the description outside the As-asked block (never comments), and the check.
- **The guard.** It sits beside the As-asked guard at both description-write call sites. When a write adds or changes the size section, it refuses with a 422 that names the line:
  - `SIZE_RECORD_HOW`: a file path, a code span, call syntax or a numbered step. A quotation that matches the As-asked block word for word is exempt.
  - `SIZE_RECORD_POLICY_CUT`: "the standing policy" deciding "wrong work".
  - `SIZE_RECORD_DROPPED`: a write that drops the section.

  An unchanged section never blocks a write. The codes are documented beside AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE.
- **Close-out keeps the record.** The prune step keeps the section verbatim.
- **The policy.** The workspace preference `sizePolicy` (`ask` / `err-larger`) is stored with who set it and when. It is set from Settings → Running, which asks why, records it in the change log and offers Undo. The area's state names it. One loader feeds every path that renders a scoping prompt.
- **The facts line.** The selector's trail facts gain "Size of the move: …".

**Evidence**
- **New tests:** 38 in three files, plus Settings route and census tests.
- **Finding 9 fixtures:** the hand-offs from LIN-4178, LIN-4251 and LIN-4252, verbatim. All three are refused on every line that carried how.
- **Seen failing first:** every new behavioural test fails against base code. Ten mutations (the guard removed, the prune line removed, the facts line removed, both edges of the quote exemption, the policy-cut check, the dropped check, the unchanged-section skip, the parser scope, and the policy dropped from the override arm) were each caught by a named test.
- **Full local unit suite:** 24207/24207.

**Cuts to the As-asked block:** none. Changes of course are noted on LIN-4346.

## Review — LIN-4368

Reviewed PR #2355 (https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2355) at head `e91d62c0`, based on `9c2a378a` (LIN-4367). `origin/main` has not moved since then. The PR is mergeable (CLEAN).

CI: green on `e91d62c0`: unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan and `ci-success`.

**Changes of course** (from the comment on LIN-4346 at 23:55). I checked all three against the code and accept them:
- four scoping render paths instead of two;
- the policy goes in the change log, with Undo;
- the Running state always names the policy.

There are no cuts to the As-asked block, and no rulings exist on this anchor.

### Against what was asked, in order
- **One module owns the record.** Met. `lib/size-of-move.js` holds the heading, the five sizes, the decided-by values and a parser that reads `outsideAsAsked` only, never comments. The guard, the facts line, the prune line, the policy line and Settings all import from it.
- **What a record says.** Met as vocabulary (`RECORD_PARTS`). Piece 3 is what writes records.
- **The guard.** Met at both call sites in `routes/proxy-writes.js`, after `refusedByAsAsked`. The 422 names the line. The three codes are documented beside AS_ASKED_IMMUTABLE. An unchanged section passes. The session lane is untouched. **One gap (fix 2 below):** the "policy decides wrong work" check reads only the first section.
- **Close-out keeps the record.** Met. The prune step keeps the section verbatim, and a prune that drops it gets `SIZE_RECORD_DROPPED`.
- **The policy.** Met for storage: `sizePolicy` is stored as `{value, setBy, setAt}` beside `dispatchDefaults`. Met for Settings → Running: the route is in the census, the state is shown, and changes ask why, log, and offer Undo. **Not fully met for "one loader… so both scoping-render paths carry it" (fix 1 below):** a fifth render path that dispatches does not call the loader.
- **Facts line.** Met. `- Size of the move: not recorded / pending a ruling / chosen X (by …)`. The router fixtures were regenerated, and the ceiling reason is recorded.

### Regression check
`git log -30` on the touched files shows only LIN-4367 and LIN-4352/4345 work. The As-asked guard still runs first, and its refusal is unchanged. The prompt-size ceilings follow LIN-4367's new shape: the latest reason sits beside the ceiling, and the history is under `## Ceiling history`. No reverted change is re-applied.

### Test quality and mutation check (LIN-2274)
The four new and touched test files pass (120/120 together with the census, change-log and budget tests). I ran eight mutations, and a named test caught each one. I reverted every mutation afterwards.
- M1: guard removed at the merged-body site. 4 tests fail.
- M2: guard removed at the PATCH site. The proxy-lane test fails.
- M3: policy removed from `prepareRecommendationInput`. 2 tests fail.
- M4: prune keep-line removed. The close-out test fails.
- M5: quote exemption made always true. The "same span not in the ask is refused" test fails.
- M6: policy line removed from the scoping template. 5 tests fail.
- M7: policy removed from `/api/proxy/prompt` in proxy-compute. Its entrance test fails.
- M8: dropped-section check removed. The `SIZE_RECORD_DROPPED` test fails.

The guard tests drive real proxy HTTP routes, not spies, which is the right level.

**Probes.** Plain prose, "and/or", "e.g.", version numbers, URLs, ticket refs, bullet options and a quoted ask span all pass. "Node.js" is refused as a path, which matches the stated lean towards refusing; not a finding.

### One of a class?
**Class: places that render a scoping prompt must carry the standing policy.** The PR covers four paths: `prepareRecommendationInput`, the override arm in `dispatch-entrance`, and proxy-compute `/prompt` and `/recommend?kind=`. A fifth is unhandled and **inside** the ticket's bounded class ("One loader … so both scoping-render paths carry it"; the PR's comment claims "every path"):

- `routes/workspace-api-prompts.js:259`, `GET /workspace/:urlKey/api/prompt/:issueId/:labelName`.
  - This is the route the UI's "run a step now" uses (`public/prompt-section.js:1820` → `window.dispatchPrompt`), and the prompt panel uses it too.
  - It builds `context` without `sizePolicy`. So in a workspace set to `err-larger`, a scoping run started from the UI is dispatched with "no standing policy".
  - Ledger item 1.

The guard is one class with two call sites, both covered. Isolated otherwise.

### Fixes for close-out to make
1. **`routes/workspace-api-prompts.js`**
   - Add `workspacePreferencesStore` to `createPromptsRoutes`' deps, and pass it at `routes/workspace-api.js:217`, where it is already in scope.
   - In the non-test, non-custom branch, set `context.sizePolicy = await loadSizePolicy(workspacePreferencesStore, workspace.urlKey)` before `generatePrompt`.
   - Add a case to `tests/unit/size-policy-render.test.js`: `GET /workspace/:k/api/prompt/:id/scoping` shows the err-larger line when the policy is set, and "no standing policy" when it is not.
   - Confirm the case fails with the loader call removed.
2. **`lib/size-of-move.js` `checkSizeRecord`.** The policy-cut test reads `readSizeRecord(next)`, which is only the first section. Make it check every section in `after`: refuse if any section's Size is "wrong work" and its Decided by is the standing policy.
   - Repro: a live record, plus a second `## Size of the move` section added with `**Size:** wrong work` / `**Decided by:** the standing policy`. Today this returns `{ok:true}`; it should return `SIZE_RECORD_POLICY_CUT`.
   - Add that as a test.

Nit, not blocking: the Running state's "No run · larger" reads as "no run" rather than "no runner". If 16 characters allow it, "No runner·larger" (no spaces around the dot) would be clearer. Leave it if not.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (policy loader class, "both scoping-render paths carry it"). The in-app `/api/prompt/:id/scoping` route, used by the UI's run-step press, renders without the policy. Settle **before the merge** with fix 1 and its test. What tells right from wrong: with `sizePolicy = {value:'err-larger'}` stored, the rendered scoping prompt contains `**Standing size policy:** err larger`, not "no standing policy".
- **Inside** (the guard: "the standing policy" deciding "wrong work"). The policy-cut check skips a second section. Settle **before the merge** with fix 2 and its test (repro above).
- **Inside** (Settings → Running sets the policy). No E2E drives the real form round trip: ask why → save → change-log row → Undo. Unit route tests cover the handlers. Settle **after the deploy** with a live check:
  - set "Err larger" with a reason in Settings → Running;
  - confirm the sidebar reads "Ready · larger" (or "No run · larger"), and the change log shows "Size of the move: err larger";
  - press Undo and confirm it returns to "ask";
  - set it back to err-larger, as John's standing answer.
- **Outside**, already owned by LIN-4369 (Todo): no producer writes a size record yet, so the guard and the facts line run on fixtures only. LIN-4369's pre-registered replay is its discharge; nothing to file.
- **Rollback.** Revert the squash commit of PR #2355. A stored `preferences.sizePolicy` key is additive, and old code ignores it, so the change is reversible.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## Close-out — LIN-4368

**Merged:** PR [#2355](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2355), squash commit `eeda7e44` on `main`, merged pinned to CI-green head `d16c5d2e`. **Deployed:** the harbour.cat footer shows `eeda7e44`, and Railway's "Harbour / production" deploy succeeded.

**How it meets what was asked:** as review found (comment of 23:59). One module owns the record vocabulary, parser and check. The guard covers both description-write sites and its codes are documented. The close-out prune keeps the section verbatim. `sizePolicy` is stored with who set it and when. Settings → Running sets it, logs the change and offers Undo. The facts line is in place. The two gaps review found are now fixed (below).

### Changes made after the approval (all in commit `d16c5d2e`)
1. **Fix 1: the policy reaches the in-app prompt route.** This answers the review's "Fixes 1" and ledger item 1. `routes/workspace-api-prompts.js` now takes `workspacePreferencesStore`, passed from `routes/workspace-api.js`, and sets `context.sizePolicy` from `loadSizePolicy` before `generatePrompt`; custom prompts are left as they were. A new test in `tests/unit/size-policy-render.test.js` drives `GET /workspace/:k/api/prompt/:id/scoping` on a real (non-test-token) workspace with a fake provider. It shows the err-larger line when the policy is set and "no standing policy" when it is not. It fails when the loader call is removed, and also when the store isn't passed in `workspace-api.js`; both mutations were reverted.
2. **Fix 2: every size section is checked for a policy cut.** This answers "Fixes 2" and ledger item 2. `checkSizeRecord` in `lib/size-of-move.js` now reads each section in `after`, through a shared `recordOf` that `readSizeRecord` also uses. A new test in `tests/unit/size-of-move.test.js` takes a valid live record, appends a second section with `**Size:** wrong work` / `**Decided by:** the standing policy`, and expects `SIZE_RECORD_POLICY_CUT`. It fails against the old code.
3. **The review's nit.** The Running state now reads "No runner·larger" (16 characters, exactly `STATE_MAX_LENGTH`) instead of "No run · larger". The comment and two test assertions were updated to match.
4. **A citation the fix made stale.** The `loadSizePolicy` docstring in `lib/workspace-preferences.js` now names the in-app prompt route among its callers.

### Ledger
- **Inside: the in-app route renders without the policy.** Settled before the merge by fix 1 and its test, which exercises the exact precondition review named (stored `err-larger` gives `**Standing size policy:** err larger`).
- **Inside: the policy-cut check skipped a second section.** Settled before the merge by fix 2 and its test, which uses review's repro.
- **Inside: Settings → Running real-form round trip.** **Not run.** The close-out session had no signed-in browser on harbour.cat, and the proxy has no size-policy write. Recorded on the PR ([comment](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2355#issuecomment-6715000201)). **For the operator (John):** in Settings → Running, set "Err larger" with a reason; check the sidebar reads "Ready · larger" (or "No runner·larger") and the change log shows "Size of the move: err larger"; press Undo and check it returns to "ask"; then set err-larger again as the standing answer. *Note: production currently has no standing policy*, so until someone sets it, scoping prompts read "no standing policy".
- **Outside: no producer writes a size record yet.** Already owned by LIN-4369, which discharges it with its pre-registered replay. Nothing filed.
- **Rollback:** as review named it, revert squash commit `eeda7e44`. The stored `preferences.sizePolicy` key is additive and old code ignores it.

### Live checks on what landed (`eeda7e44`, production)
- `GET /api/proxy/prompt/LIN-4369/scoping` carries `**Standing size policy:** no standing policy; the size of the move is a person's ruling.`
- `description/append` of a size section containing a file path is refused with 422 `SIZE_RECORD_HOW`, naming line 6 and the path.
- `description/append` of a size section with "wrong work" decided by the standing policy is refused with 422 `SIZE_RECORD_POLICY_CUT`. LIN-4368 had no existing section, so this was a sole section; the second-section case is covered by the new unit test.
- Neither refused write changed the description. The three `SIZE_RECORD_*` codes appear in `/api/proxy/instructions`.

### CI
Green on `d16c5d2e`: unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan and `ci-success`. The local full unit suite passes 24209/24209 (24207 before, plus the two new tests).

### Related tickets
- **LIN-4369** (3/4): unblocked. Piece 2's record, guard and policy are live.
- **LIN-4346:** this piece is done. Pieces 3 and 4 stay open.
- **Follow-ups filed:** none. The only outside item is already owned by LIN-4369. No rulings were raised.
